note: Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them. Hidden flags follow the published split: 12 story trophies and 16 other hidden trophies, 28 hidden in all. Counts are the targets the official descriptions state, or the counts the published trophy lists give. Every guide is written for this entry, in our own words, and cites its sources.

trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one unlocks by itself — there is no separate task behind it. Work through the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles, the activities and the 100% checklist, and the platinum is the last thing you hear. Published guides put the whole run at around 200 hours, most of it on the 100% checklist, so treat this as the finish line, not a trophy to chase on its own.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade, as listed before this bounty opened
EGamers, reporting PowerPyx — about 200 hours for the platinum, difficulty 4 out of 10

trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion. This is the long one, and the hardest trophy on the list: the full 100% checklist only opens up once the story's credits have rolled, so most of this trophy is post-story work. The checklist covers the story, the collectibles, the challenges and the map — use the roadmap's last stage as your list and tick each part off there. Published guides put the platinum run at about 200 hours, and most of that time sits here. Our own advice: the official description gives no breakdown of the checklist, so follow the in-game list when it opens.

sources: Exophase — official name, description and grade
HowToVideoGame — the full 100% checklist opens after the story
EGamers, reporting PowerPyx — A Long Road is the hardest trophy; about 200 hours for the platinum

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, airtime and near-miss driving the game counts as you play — the target of 250 is in the official description, so any stunt that registers adds to it. Do them as you travel between missions rather than grinding all 250 at once: fast cars, ramps and jumps around Leonida all feed the same counter. Our own advice, from the official description: the exact moves that count as a stunt are not pinned down yet, so watch the in-game counter.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. There are 9 activity types, per HowToVideoGame — fishing, races, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, drone races, meditation, hunting and the rest of the side activities the game offers. Play one of each and the trophy pops; you do not need to win or finish any of them, just try them. Use the checklist to tick each type off as you try it.

Learn one range at a time, chase gold on each before moving on, and use the checklist to mark each gold as you earn it. Our own advice: the ranges' layouts and scoring are not pinned down yet, so the in-game range menu is the authority on what each challenge asks.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. The published list counts 8 garage properties — buy every one. Garages are bought with cash, so this trophy follows your money: earn, save and buy them as they appear. Our own advice: the eight garages' places and prices are not pinned down yet.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Scooter Bros app takes vehicle registrations — register 10 different vehicles through it. Discover a vehicle, open the app and register it; ten registrations pop the trophy. Our own advice: the app's steps are not pinned down yet — HowToVideoGame's Scooter Bros guide is the place to check.
